question: What was the main belief about the cause of mental illness in ancient times?
explanation: Ancient societies lacked medical knowledge and attributed strange or erratic behaviors to supernatural forces and evil spirits. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h1)

question: What was the purpose of trephining in ancient societies?

options.A: To let trapped evil spirits escape the skull
options.B: To relieve pressure from a physical head injury
options.C: To deliver herbal medicines directly to tissue
options.D: To lower high blood pressure in the brain

explanation: Healers cut holes in the skull believing it created a physical exit door for the demons causing the mental illness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h1)

question: What was the primary goal of early psychiatric asylums?

options.A: To isolate patients and protect public safety
options.B: To rehabilitate individuals for quick discharge
options.C: To provide advanced psychotherapy and counseling

explanation: Early asylums functioned mainly to lock away people with mental illness to keep them out of the general community. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h2)

question: How were patients typically treated inside early asylums?

options.B: Involved in daily group therapy sessions
options.C: Given regular rest periods and nutritious meals
options.D: Chained, neglected, and viewed as public spectacles

explanation: Conditions were brutal, and facilities even charged admission fees for tourists to come and stare at the inmates. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h2)

question: Who was a key pioneer of the Moral Treatment movement in France?
explanation: Philippe Pinel famously ordered the chains removed from patients in Paris asylums and introduced humane treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: What was the core belief of the Moral Treatment movement?

options.A: Mental illness should be met with kindness and a peaceful environment
options.B: Patients must be permanently separated from society
options.C: Strict physical punishment is necessary to cure madness
options.D: Spiritual exorcisms are the only true cure for mental disorders

explanation: Moral treatment shifted care away from cruelty and towards dignity, fresh air, useful work, and compassionate human interaction. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which theorist developed the system of psychoanalysis?
explanation: Sigmund Freud created psychoanalysis, focusing on the unconscious mind and early childhood experiences. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h4)

question: What was the main focus of early psychoanalytic therapy?

options.A: Isolating patients from stressful family environments
options.B: Training patients to change bad habits through rewards
options.C: Exploring hidden conflicts in the unconscious mind
options.D: Using electrical shocks to reset brain chemistry

explanation: Psychoanalysis aimed to bring repressed memories and hidden emotional struggles from the unconscious into conscious awareness. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h4)

question: What was the first major antipsychotic medication discovered in the 1950s?
explanation: Chlorpromazine was the pioneering antipsychotic drug that revolutionized the medical management of severe psychiatric disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h5)

question: How did the introduction of psychotropic medications change inpatient psychiatric units?

options.A: It made hospitals completely empty within a single year
options.B: It calmed acute symptoms, making patients more responsive to therapy
options.C: It caused patients to lose all of their memories permanently
options.D: It completely eliminated the need for psychiatric nurses

explanation: Drugs reduced severe agitation and psychosis, allowing patients to participate meaningfully in rehabilitation programs. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h5)

question: What was the primary goal of the deinstitutionalization movement?

options.A: To replace all psychiatric nurses with automated machines
options.B: To move patients from large asylums into community-based care
options.C: To stop using medications entirely in mental health
options.D: To build bigger and more secure state hospitals

explanation: Deinstitutionalization aimed to shut down giant warehouses and treat patients closer to home with outpatient support. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h6)

question: What was a major negative consequence when asylums closed too quickly?

options.A: Many vulnerable patients became homeless or ended up in prison
options.B: Mental illnesses disappeared completely from society
options.C: Families refused to ever speak to psychiatric nurses again
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies stopped making all psychiatric drugs

explanation: Because local community clinics lacked proper funding, many discharged patients fell through the cracks of society. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h6)

question: Who is famously known as the mother of psychiatric nursing for her work on interpersonal relations?
explanation: Hildegard Peplau developed the theory of interpersonal relations, defining the therapeutic role of the nurse in psychiatric care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h7)

question: What was the early nature of psychiatric facilities like the Yaba Lunatic Asylum when first opened?

options.A: Private luxury retreats for wealthy politicians
options.B: Holistic herbal healing camps run by local traditional leaders
options.C: Advanced community wellness centers with modern psychotherapy
options.D: Custodial holding centers modeled after harsh colonial asylums

explanation: Early colonial facilities in Nigeria were primarily designed for confinement and public safety rather than therapeutic rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h7)
